facts.fact: TechAfrica News reports that NITDA has introduced a four-part cloud policy package whose National Cloud Computing Guideline drives a Cloud First mandate across government institutions; the article gives no issue date, so its published date is used.

NITDA's director-general said Nigeria operates under a newly institutionalised Cloud-First Policy that consolidates public sector IT spending, and referred to the National Digital Cloud Policy as being activated; the article gives no adoption date, so its published date is used.

TechCabal reports that on Monday 17 August 2026 the Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy released the National Digital Cloud Policy, which makes cloud the default deployment model for federal ministries, departments and agencies for new systems and requires phased migration plans.

TechCabal reports that the National Digital Cloud Policy supersedes the Nigeria Cloud Computing Policy 2019, which first introduced the Cloud First principle and was implemented unevenly according to the new policy.

TechCabal reports that under the policy Galaxy Backbone Limited will aggregate government cloud demand from registered providers and negotiate framework agreements, with procurement through a National Digital Marketplace on which NITDA handles provider registration; a 24-month roadmap plans migration of priority ministries in months six to twelve, with no migration yet reported.

facts.fact: The Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy announced it has unveiled the National Digital Cloud Policy, which implements a strengthened Cloud First approach across federal ministries, departments and agencies with whole-of-government aggregation and shared government cloud services.

A law-firm review on Mondaq says Nigeria has issued the National Digital Cloud Policy, whose Parts I, II and IV (investment, government adoption, implementation) take effect on publication while Part III, the sovereignty framework, takes effect only on Presidential approval; the article gives no issue date, so its published date is used.
The review says the National Digital Cloud Policy replaces the 2019 Nigeria Cloud Computing Policy; the article gives no replacement date, so its published date is used.

The review says Part II designates Galaxy Backbone Limited the primary digital infrastructure provider, aggregating government cloud demand and operating shared government platforms, with procurement through a National Digital Marketplace on which only certified providers may be listed; the article gives no date for the designation, so its published date is used.

facts.fact: BusinessDay states that NITDA's National Cloud Computing Policy was first issued in 2019 and established a Cloud First approach for government institutions.

Punch reports that Nigeria introduced a Cloud First policy in 2019 to discourage ministries, departments and agencies from building separate data centres and to encourage use of cloud services.

Punch quotes NITDA Director-General Kashifu Inuwa saying the existing Cloud First policy remains in force and that government agencies are not prohibited from using international public cloud platforms; published 2026-08-12.

Punch reports, quoting Inuwa, that NITDA's consultation process has produced three guidelines covering data classification and cloud policy, minimum requirements for cloud service providers, and digital quality assurance; no date is given, so the published date 2026-08-12 is used.

The NITDA director-general, speaking at ITW Data Cloud Africa 2026 in Nairobi, referred to the National Digital Cloud Policy and its investment roadmap, and to a National Cloud Infrastructure Strategy, as existing instruments expected to give investors clarity; the article gives no adoption date, so the published date is used.

The NITDA director-general said Nigeria's National Digital Cloud Policy and its investment roadmap are intended to reduce barriers to private-sector participation, and that the National Cloud Infrastructure Strategy turns regulatory requirements into contracted demand; the article gives no adoption date, so the published date is used.
